task_message:
Case L29: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 161x161x173 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case L29 complete.

**What I did**
- Reviewed the volume in all three planes (axial, sagittal, coronal sheets plus targeted slices) to locate the abnormality.
- Identified the target as the T2-hyperintense, spindle/teardrop-shaped fatty mass in the anterior subcutaneous–fascial compartment of the limb (bulbous bright core with tapering fatty extensions along the fascia), distinct from the thin normal subcutaneous fat elsewhere.
- Seeded the model on the mass on axial slice 60, then reviewed the result in three planes and expanded it along the contiguous fatty extension (accepted contiguous candidate tissue), finally filling internal holes.
- Verified the final extent on the five-slice-per-plane review: the past-the-mask slices showed no residual lesion tissue, no stray components; remaining small intensity proposals were thin normal fat/fascial stripes and were rejected.

**Final result**: single-component mask, 39.7 mL, axial extent 23–107, coronal 90–119, sagittal 52–108, following the lesion boundary in all planes. Confidence: medium (lesion ends taper into adjacent fat, so the extreme tips are the least certain).
